steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Verfremdungseffekt (V-effect / alienation effect): making the familiar strange so the audience THINKS rather than feels — prevents emotional absorption. | Key Fact: Gestus: a combination of gesture and social attitude — reveals the character's social and political position, not their psychology. | Key Fact: Episodic structure: each scene stands alone — prevents narrative immersion, encourages critical comparison between scenes. | Key Fact: Placards and narration: tell the audience what will happen before it does — removes suspense, forces attention onto HOW and WHY.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the purpose of Brecht's alienation effect and describe three techniques he uses to achieve it. | What is gestus and how does it differ from a naturalistic approach to character? | How would you stage a scene using Brechtian techniques to make the audience think critically about a social issue?
